A new study co-authored by Dr. Denis Anikiev presents a three-dimensional lithospheric density model of the South China Sea and examines how the Hainan mantle plume may have interacted with the oceanic lithosphere.

The model integrates gravity observations with geological and geophysical constraints. The results identify a north–south density and temperature contrast across the extinct spreading axis in the eastern sub-basin, supporting a scenario in which plume material influenced asymmetric seafloor spreading through lateral flow toward the ridge.

Published in *Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth*, the work is an outcome of collaboration among researchers at Nanjing University, GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, KFUPM, and partner institutions.
